persona: Friendly and a little unsure about insurance words; calls her home policy 'mortgage insurance' because the bank arranged it with the mortgage.
initial_message: Hi, I think I need to claim on my mortgage insurance? On Wednesday 23 September my partner and I were carrying a wardrobe down the hallway and lost our grip. The corner went straight through the hallway wall and gouged the door frame. Nobody got hurt.

facts.policyholder.name: Grace Fernmoor
facts.incident.description: On Wednesday evening my partner and I were carrying a wardrobe down the hallway. We lost our grip and the corner of the wardrobe went through the hallway wall and gouged the bedroom door frame.
facts.incident.cause: Accidentally hit the wall while carrying furniture
facts.loss.description: Hole about 20 cm across through the hallway wall plasterboard; deep gouge in the bedroom door frame
facts.if_asked_who_else_was_there: My partner, Rawiri Tanewood. He lives here with me.
facts.evidence.photos: One photo of the hole and the door frame. Available now.
facts.evidence.repair_quote: Quote from Matai Shaw Construction, total $1,288.00 including GST, dated 25 September 2026. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_the_name_on_the_quote: I did not notice my name is not on it. The builder must have left it off. I can ask them for a new copy with my name.
facts.if_asked_which_policy: The house policy, NW-SYN-HOM-200021. The bank set it up with the mortgage, so I call it mortgage insurance.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo of a painted hallway wall in a house, showing a ragged hole about the size of a hand punched through the plasterboard at waist height, with crumbled white gypsum and torn paper around its edges, and a deep gouge in the white-painted timber door frame beside it. Warm evening indoor light. The frame shows the wall and the door frame only.
materials.purpose: Shows the hole in the wall and the damaged door frame

data.subject: 21 Lighthouse Test Road, Stoke, Nelson - hallway wall and bedroom door frame

items.description: Cut out and patch hallway plasterboard
Replace damaged section of bedroom door frame and architrave
Stop, sand and paint hallway wall

materials.purpose: Repair quote with the customer name left out

data.wording: Northwind Home Standard Policy, version MVP-2026.1

materials.purpose: Policy schedule that matches the home wording in the knowledge base

design.notes: Boundary: the builder quote leaves the customer name blank. The claimant calls the home policy 'mortgage insurance'; the Claim must end as home (G3).

triage.rationale: The quote has no customer name, so it cannot be tied to the policyholder and a complete copy is needed. Everything else is simple: accidental damage inside the home, nobody hurt, no other party (the partner lives in the home), total NZD 1,288.00 including GST. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: No receipt or ownership document in the pack

quote_before_loss.basis: Quote dated 25 September 2026; incident 23 September 2026. The missing field is the customer name, not the date.

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 April 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2020-04-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.
